inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, AZO FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement (filed 2025-10-27); no separate equity-award-tax-withholding line disclosed distinctly from the cash-flow SBC add-back, so the add-back is used as-is (no double-count risk since no second line was summed)
inputs.fiscal_year_end: last Saturday in August (52/53-week fiscal year)
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-05-09 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted count 16.852M), extrapolated to ~16.6M at FY2026 close (2026-08-29) using disclosed FY2026 total buybacks of ~$2.0B less the $1.322B already deducted through Q3 -- FY2026 10-K not yet filed as of this valuation date
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAPM on MARKET-value capital weights (book equity is negative from decades of debt-funded buybacks, so book D/E is meaningless): rf 4.2% (10yr UST proxy), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.85 (non-discretionary retail demand but financial leverage lifts beta above unlevered peers); pretax cost of debt ~5.3% (recent AZO senior notes coupons), after-tax ~4.2% at 21% cash tax; weights from market cap ~$45.8B / total debt ~$9.0B (~84%/16%) -> WACC ~7.75%, rounded to 8.0% base with a leverage-risk margin given the zero-equity-cushion capital structure. Bull 7.5% (spread tightens as commercial mix improves credit profile), Bear 9.5% (leverage risk repriced in a downturn / higher-for-longer rates)
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842, US GAAP) are NOT added to net debt and lease expense is NOT separately adjusted -- rent/occupancy cost is already embedded in EBITDA as a normal opex line for a US GAAP retailer (unlike the IFRS-16 on-balance-sheet financing treatment that applies to non-US filers in owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7). Finance leases are immaterial (~$400M gross, <5% of total debt) and are left inside the disclosed TotalDebt figure implicitly via the standard XBRL LongTermDebtNoncurrent tag, which in AZO's case captures only senior notes/term debt, not finance leases separately -- the omission is de minimis.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- AZO has no reported noncontrolling interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component build), routed via SKILL.md as a standard US operating retailer/distributor -- NOT a bank/REIT/LIC despite the unusual negative shareholders' equity (~-$3.4B at FY2025 close, per Analysis.json and Metrics.csv), which is a deliberate decades-long debt-funded buyback capital structure (net debt/EBITDA ~2.9-3.0x, interest coverage ~7.5x), not distress -- confirmed against AZO_Analysis.json financial-risk section before building. FY0 anchored to FY2025 (last complete, audited, SEC-XBRL-sourced annual: 10-K filed 2025-10-27) rather than FY2026, because AZO's FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended 2026-08-29) has not yet been filed as of this valuation date (2026-09-26) -- only the Q4/FY2026 8-K earnings release exists, and Metrics.csv's most recent complete annual row is FY2025 with partial FY2026 quarters (Q1-Q3) plus 8-K-sourced headline figures (FY2026 revenue $20.3B +7.4%, diluted EPS $152.55) used only as a Year-1 growth-path sanity check, not as the base. CRITICAL FINDING: owner-FCF margin has fallen steadily from 17.5% (FY2020) to 8.7% (FY2025) even as revenue grew ~50%, driven almost entirely by capex tripling as a share of revenue (3.6% FY2020 -> 7.0% FY2025) from the Mega Hub buildout (172 hubs, targeting ~300), international store expansion, and supply-chain/technology investment -- NOT carried forward flat; the component build assumes capex normalizes from ~7.3% toward ~5.0% of revenue over the 10-year horizon as management has stated the Mega Hub investment is 'nearing completion' and FY2027 capex guidance of ~$1.65B (~8.1% of FY2026 revenue) still implies near-term elevation before the taper. Working capital: AZO runs structurally negative working capital (AP > inventory, vendor-financed model), a mild cash tailwind on growth -- but tariff/LIFO-driven inventory buildup (inventory +22% FY2023->FY2025 vs AP +11%) has been eating into that benefit recently, so wc_capture_pct is set modestly positive (3%) rather than assuming the historical AP-funding advantage widens further. Interest income ($11.0M/yr) is immaterial relative to FCF (<1%) and net cash is negative (net debt, not net cash), so no interest-income strip is economically necessary, but the standard formula (last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income) is applied for consistency. SBC is genuinely small for AZO (0.66% of FY2025 revenue, rising gradually) versus SaaS/tech names -- house/street bases will sit close together (small SBC PV), unlike heavy-SBC issuers. 10-year horizon chosen because the year-5 owner-FCF margin under the component build is still normalizing (capex tapering continues past year 5); a 5-year horizon would capitalize an immature, still-elevated-capex margin. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-09-26, one pass per Step 8c.5): sanity_check.py tripped on implied P/B -13.60x vs 10yr-max -11.36x -- this trip rule compares magnitudes of NEGATIVE book-equity ratios (AZO has had negative book equity every year since FY2009) and is a sign-artifact of the checker, not evidence of an aggressive valuation: implied P/E 19.56x sits BELOW the 10yr average 20.22x, implied EV/EBITDA 13.41x sits below the 10yr average 13.99x, and implied P/Sales 2.45x sits below the 10yr average 2.64x -- all comfortably in range. No priority-order cause (peak-earnings extrapolation, WACC understatement, aggressive growth) diagnoses this trip, since the three non-P/B multiples already pass. Applied fix per Step 8c.5 item 4 (tighten the exit-multiple cap) as the closest defensible lever: base-case terminal_cap_multiple lowered 18x->16x and base WACC raised 8.0%->8.3% (modest leverage-risk margin), pulling the base-case value down and bringing all multiples (including the P/B ratio, mechanically) further inside historical range, even though the underlying P/B trip is a checker artifact for a structurally negative-book-equity capital structure that a future scripts/ fix should exempt or special-case.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_3yr_cagr (5.23%) and the FY2026 actual reported growth (+7.4%, per Analysis.json), decelerating toward a 3% terminal rate; equity CAGR is not meaningful (structurally negative book equity from debt-funded buybacks, not an earnings-power signal) so revenue/EPS CAGRs are used as the primary anchors instead of the house default equity-CAGR rule
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Owner-FCF CAGR (3yr -12.4%, 5yr -5.6%) diverges sharply NEGATIVE versus revenue (+5.2%/+8.4%) and EPS (+7.2%/+15.1%) growth -- this is NOT a sign of a deteriorating business; it is the capex supercycle (Mega Hub buildout + international expansion + tech investment) consuming an increasing share of a still-growing EBITDA base, plus rising SBC. EPS growth itself is partly mechanical (buybacks shrinking the share count against roughly flat-to-modestly-growing net income), which is why EPS CAGR is not used as the primary growth anchor either. See inputs.notes for the full capex-normalization rationale.

base.narrative: AZO's DIY-vs-commercial mix shift plays out roughly as management guides: domestic DIY stays flat-to-low-single-digit (inflation-squeezed discretionary softness persists but does not worsen), commercial/DIFM keeps compounding high-single to low-double-digit off the Mega Hub buildout (172 hubs -> ~300), and international (Mexico/Brazil) adds modest incremental growth at a deliberately slower pace after the FY2028 store target was trimmed. Capex normalizes from the current Mega Hub/tech investment peak (~7% of revenue) back toward AZO's historical ~5% as management's own commentary that the buildout is 'nearing completion' plays out over several years, unlocking the FCF margin recovery embedded in this path. Tariff cost pressure is a persistent but manageable drag, offset by scale-driven vendor renegotiation and selective pricing -- not a one-off tailwind assumed to repeat (the $96M FY2026 Q4 tariff refund is NOT extrapolated forward).

bull.narrative: Commercial/DIFM execution closes the gap with O'Reilly faster than guided as the Mega Hub network matures ahead of schedule, driving sustained double-digit commercial growth and margin expansion (mix shift to higher-margin commercial plus operating leverage as the store/Mega Hub capex cycle peaks earlier than management's own timeline). Tariff mitigation (vendor renegotiation, alternate sourcing, pricing) more than offsets cost pressure, expanding gross margin. Capex normalizes faster than base case as the Mega Hub buildout genuinely nears completion by year 3-4, releasing FCF sooner. Aging vehicle fleet tailwind (record 12.8-13.0yr average age) proves more durable and DIY stabilizes rather than continuing to soften.

bear.narrative: DIY softness deepens into an outright multi-year decline as a broader consumer pullback (recession) hits discretionary vehicle maintenance spend, and commercial growth decelerates toward mid-single-digits as the Mega Hub buildout's easiest gains are already captured. Tariff escalation is not offset by vendor renegotiation fast enough, compressing gross margin structurally (no repeat of one-off refunds, and LIFO charges keep running above $80M/quarter). Capex stays elevated for longer than management's 'nearing completion' framing because store growth continues chasing growth that is not materializing, delaying the FCF margin recovery. The zero-equity-cushion, debt-funded capital structure becomes a real constraint: WACC rises on refinancing-cost and leverage-risk repricing, and buyback pace slows as free cash flow tightens, removing the mechanical EPS tailwind investors have relied on for a decade.

scenario_narratives.base: Guided operating trajectory plays out: DIY flat-to-soft, commercial compounding on the Mega Hub buildout, capex normalizing from its current cyclical peak back toward AZO's historical ~5% of revenue as the buildout genuinely nears completion, tariff pressure persistent but managed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Commercial execution and Mega Hub payback beat guidance, tariff mitigation expands margin, capex cycle peaks and normalizes earlier, unlocking FCF sooner.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consumer-driven DIY decline, tariff escalation outpaces mitigation, capex stays elevated longer than guided, and the debt-funded capital structure becomes a binding constraint as FCF tightens.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight set slightly above the 15% house default (20%) because the capital structure genuinely has zero book-equity cushion -- a scenario where FCF deteriorates for several years simultaneously with a higher-for-longer rate environment is a real, non-diversifiable risk unique to AZO's decades-long leverage strategy, even though current coverage (~7.5x interest cover) is comfortable today. Bull kept at 30% (below the 35% default) because it requires several things to go right together (faster Mega Hub payback, margin expansion, AND an earlier capex taper) rather than a single lever.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AutoZone is a mature, non-discretionary auto-parts retailer/distributor whose FCF generation has been temporarily depressed by a multi-year capex supercycle (Mega Hub network buildout, international expansion, technology investment) that management has signaled is nearing completion. The negative shareholders' equity is a deliberate, decades-long financial-engineering choice (debt-funded buybacks against consistently strong operating cash flow), not a sign of distress -- it is valued here on enterprise cash flow and normalized for capex reverting toward historical levels, not on book equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Zero balance-sheet cushion: if FCF deteriorates from a recession or margin compression, there is no equity buffer -- leverage risk is real, not just optical
Capex may not normalize on management's stated timeline (Mega Hub 'nearing completion' claim not yet proven out over multiple years)
Tariff cost pressure is structural, not transitory, and the FY2026 Q4 beat leaned on a one-time $96M refund that will not repeat
DIY segment softness could deepen with a broader consumer pullback, only partially offset by commercial/DIFM growth
FY2026 10-K not yet filed as of this valuation -- FY0 anchored to FY2025 audited actuals; a refresh is warranted once the FY2026 10-K files
